verdict.rationale: Intel documents an NPU alongside CPU and GPU AI engines on Core Ultra processors. It also lists official, shipping developer runtimes and tools: OpenVINO, WindowsML/DirectML, ONNX RT, WebNN, oneDNN/PyTorch optimizations, and VTune profiling for NPUs. However, the pack contains no published TOPS figure, so that half of the story is unevidenced. missing for 10: a published NPU/platform TOPS figure with stated precision (e.g., INT8), and confirmation that the SDKs target the 285K's NPU specifically rather than the CPU, plus independent hands-on corroboration of developer access to the NPU.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, the chip's AI acceleration is exposed to developers — an NPU or neural engine with a published TOPS figure (precision stated) and an official SDK or runtime that ships today

citations.quote: AI acceleration is built into every Intel® Core™ Ultra processor, with three AI engines—CPU, GPU, and NPU—all working together to support the next era of AI software.
AI Software Frameworks Supported by CPU OpenVINO™, WindowsML, DirectML, ONNX RT, WebNN
Optimize performance on client GPUs and NPUs from Intel with new analysis tool features in Intel® VTune™ Profiler.

Maximize AI PC inference capabilities from large language models (LLM) to image generation with Intel® oneAPI Deep Neural Network Library (oneDNN) and PyTorch optimizations for Intel® Core™ Ultra processors (series 2) and Intel® Arc™ GPUs.
